messages.content:
How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide that shows you how to **generate a RESTful API request** for the *“Get information of device connector versions”* endpoint in **Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1**. I’ll cover both the **web‑UI (API Explorer)** and a **command‑line (curl)** approach, plus the authentication and header details you’ll need. --- ## 1. Find the Endpoint in the Dashboard | Item | What to look for | Where to find it | |------|------------------|------------------| | **Base URL** | `https:///api/v1` | Dashboard → *Help → API Reference* | | **Endpoint** | `/device-connector-versions` (GET) | API Reference → “Device Connector Versions” | | **Query Parameters** | `deviceId`, `connectorType`, `version`, `limit`, `offset` (optional) | Same page | | **Response** | JSON array of connector‑version objects | Same page | > **Tip:** If you can’t find the exact path, use the *API Explorer* (see below) – it will auto‑populate the URL. --- ## 2. Authentication Cisco Nexus Dashboard uses **OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens** for API calls. | Step | Action | |------|--------| | 1 | Log in to the Dashboard UI. | | 2 | Go to **User Settings → API Tokens** (or **Admin → API Tokens**). | | 3 | Click **Generate Token**. | | 4 | Copy the token; it will look like `eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...`. | > **Security note:** Keep the token secret. It grants full API access until you revoke it. --- ## 3. Using the Built‑in API Explorer (Web UI) 1. **Open the Dashboard** and log in. 2. Click the **“API Explorer”** icon (usually a magnifying glass or “API” tab). 3. In the left pane, expand **“Device Connector Versions”**. 4. Select **GET /device-connector-versions**. 5. Fill in any query parameters you need (e.g., `deviceId=12345`). 6. Click **“Generate Request”**. 7. The right pane will show the full HTTP request: ``` GET https:///api/v1/device-connector-versions?deviceId=12345 Authorization: Bearer Accept: application/json ``` 8. Click **“Send”** to execute. 9. The response panel will display the JSON payload. > **Why use the Explorer?** > • It validates the request against the schema. > • It shows you the exact headers and query parameters. > • You can copy the request into Postman or your own scripts. --- ## 4. Using `curl` (Command Line) Below is a ready‑to‑run example. Replace placeholders with your actual values. ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash # Variables BASE_URL="https:///api/v1" TOKEN="eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..." # <-- your bearer token DEVICE_ID="12345" # optional CONNECTOR_TYPE="ethernet" # optional VERSION="v1.2.3" # optional # Build query string QUERY="" [ -n "$DEVICE_ID" ] && QUERY+="deviceId=$DEVICE_ID" [ -n "$CONNECTOR_TYPE" ] && [ -n "$QUERY" ] && QUERY+="&" && QUERY+="connectorType=$CONNECTOR_TYPE" [ -n "$VERSION" ] && [ -n "$QUERY" ] && QUERY+="&" && QUERY+="version=$VERSION" # Final URL URL="$BASE_URL/device-connector-versions" [ -n "$QUERY" ] && URL+="?$QUERY" # Execute curl -sS -X GET "$URL" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ | jq . ``` ### What the script does | Step | Explanation | |------|-------------| | `BASE_URL` | Base API path. | | `TOKEN` | Your OAuth bearer token. | | Query params | Add only those you need. | | `curl` headers | `Authorization` (required), `Accept`, `Content-Type`. | | `jq .` | Pretty‑prints the JSON response (install `jq` if you don’t have it). | --- ## 5. Sample Response ```json [ { "id": "dcv-001", "deviceId": "12345", "connectorType": "ethernet", "version": "v1.2.3", "releaseDate": "2024-04-15T00:00:00Z", "status": "active", "metadata": { "checksum": "abcd1234", "sizeBytes": 1048576 } }, { "id": "dcv-002", "deviceId": "12345", "connectorType": "fiber", "version": "v2.0.0", "releaseDate": "2024-05-01T00:00:00Z", "status": "deprecated", "metadata": { "checksum": "efgh5678", "sizeBytes": 2097152 } } ] ``` --- ## 6. Common Pitfalls & Troubleshooting | Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix | |---------|--------------|-----| | `401 Unauthorized` | Token expired or missing | Regenerate token or add `Authorization: Bearer ` | | `404 Not Found` | Wrong base URL or endpoint | Verify the URL (`/api/v1/device-connector-versions`) | | `400 Bad Request` | Invalid query param value | Check the API docs for allowed values | | `500 Internal Server Error` | Dashboard issue | Contact support or retry later | --- ## 7. Automating with Python (Optional) If you prefer Python, here’s a quick snippet using `requests`: ```python import requests BASE_URL = "https:///api/v1" TOKEN = "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..." HEADERS = { "Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}", "Accept": "application/json", "Content-Type": "application/json", } params = {"deviceId": "12345"} # add more if needed resp = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/device-connector-versions", headers=HEADERS, params=params) resp.raise_for_status() print(resp.json()) ``` --- ## 8. Quick Reference Cheat Sheet | Item | Example | |------|---------| | **Base URL** | `https://nexus-dashboard.company.com/api/v1` | | **Endpoint** | `GET /device-connector-versions` | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json` | | **Query** | `?deviceId=12345&connectorType=ethernet` | | **Curl** | `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer " https://.../device-connector-versions` | --- ### Done! You now know how to generate and execute a RESTful request for the *Device Connector Versions* API in Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1. If you hit any roadblocks, double‑check the token, URL, and query parameters against the API reference. Happy querying!
